diagnosis: Working diagnosis: acute anterior STEMI due to presumed proximal LAD occlusion, with evolving haemodynamic compromise. Requires immediate emergency response in real clinical practice.
risk_assessment: Severe / emergency teaching tier; no formal score implied.

investigation_reports.ecg: ST-segment elevation in anterior precordial leads in the synthetic ECG, consistent with a STEMI pattern.
investigation_reports.serial_troponin: Initial troponin may be pending early after symptom onset; later simulated samples rise substantially. Do not delay emergency pathway selection while waiting for a biomarker when the ECG and clinical context indicate STEMI.
investigation_reports.echo: Anterior and apical regional wall-motion abnormality; reduced estimated LVEF 35% in this synthetic report.
investigation_reports.angiography: Illustrative report: acute thrombotic occlusion of proximal LAD with impaired distal flow; moderate RCA disease and non-obstructive LCx disease. A separate optional branch can add left-main/multivessel complexity after the core demo.

lesions.complexity: high-acuity culprit lesion; haemodynamic deterioration risk

pathway_review.label: Activate emergency STEMI / PCI-centre pathway and simulate immediate reperfusion assessment
supports: Persistent ischemic symptoms and STEMI-pattern ECG
pathway_review.reason: Guidelines emphasize time-critical reperfusion for STEMI. This is a simulated decision pathway, not a real-time clinical instruction.

pathway_review.label: Wait for serial troponin before escalating the STEMI pathway
against: Biomarker confirmation should not delay emergency STEMI pathway when ECG/clinical criteria are sufficient
pathway_review.reason: Critical timing trap: record delay, deterioration and debrief why waiting is unsafe in this scenario.

pathway_review.label: Treat as routine outpatient stable chest pain
against: Persistent symptoms, STEMI-pattern ECG and low blood pressure indicate emergency risk
pathway_review.reason: Critical misclassification. Block progression to a routine pathway and show a stop-level safety alert.

simulated_clinical_course.t_plus_0: Persistent pain and STEMI-pattern ECG; emergency pathway choice is time-sensitive.
simulated_clinical_course.t_plus_2: If learner delays escalation, simulated blood pressure falls and alert changes to STOP.
simulated_clinical_course.t_plus_5: If emergency pathway selected, transfer/team activation is logged; do not provide real catheter manipulation instructions.
simulated_clinical_course.post_reperfusion: Successful reference branch: simulated flow improves, symptoms lessen and haemodynamics stabilize with ongoing monitoring. Alternate branch: reperfusion failure or ventricular arrhythmia event triggers team-response simulation and debrief.

learning_objectives: Recognize a STEMI emergency pattern and prioritize escalation.
Understand that biomarker results may lag and should not delay an indicated emergency pathway.
Practice team communication, pre-procedure safety checks, complication recognition and post-reperfusion monitoring.
review_note: Synthetic content requires review and approval by a qualified interventional cardiologist before educational deployment. No values are validated clinical thresholds or instructions.
